analysis.one_liner: State Bank of India is the country's largest bank by assets, majority-owned by the Government of India, running retail and corporate banking alongside stakes in insurance, cards and mutual fund subsidiaries.
analysis.whats_happening: SBI reported Q2 FY27 (quarter ended Sep 2026) results on 3 November 2026: standalone net profit of ₹23,038 crore, up 14.28% year-on-year, with net interest income up 14.69% to ₹49,143 crore and gross NPAs falling to 1.39%, said to be the lowest in roughly two decades. Despite this, the stock fell around 5% in the days after results as some metrics missed street expectations, and MarketsMojo downgraded it to 'Sell' on valuation grounds on 4 November 2026. No confirmed date for Q3 FY27 results, dividend record date or AGM was found; the next results are estimated for early February 2027 based on last year's pattern, but this is not confirmed - check NSE/BSE filings closer to the date.
analysis.plain_terms: A bank's core business is borrowing cheap (deposits) and lending at a markup (loans) - that spread is the Net Interest Margin, which improved slightly to 3.11% domestically this quarter. The encouraging part is that bad loans, measured by Gross NPA, have fallen to 1.39%, a two-decade low, and the bank set aside less money for potential losses than a year ago. The tension: even with these improving numbers, the stock fell after results and one brokerage called it a 'Sell' on valuation - meaning good operating performance and a favourable market view on the price don't always move together, and some of SBI's profitability metrics (like ROE) disagree significantly across data sources.
analysis.quarters: Q2 FY27 (Sep 2026): PAT ₹23,038 crore (+14.28% YoY), NII ₹49,143 crore (+14.69% YoY), operating profit ₹34,226 crore (+7.8% YoY). Domestic NIM rose to 3.11% from 3.00% in Q1 FY27 and 3.08% a year earlier. Gross NPA fell to 1.39% from 1.73% YoY; Net NPA fell to 0.36% from 0.42% YoY. Provisions dropped to ₹4,217 crore from ₹5,400 crore YoY, and credit cost fell to 0.22% from 0.39% YoY. Management (Chairman C.S. Setty) guided to 14-15% credit growth and 10-11% deposit growth for FY27, and said NIM should stay above 3% for the year, with growth 'well diversified' across retail, agri, SME and corporate books. These figures are corroborated across multiple independent reports and the concall itself, so confidence in this quarter's numbers is high.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is up 15.82% over 1 year versus Nifty's -2.9% and flat returns from peer Bank of Baroda, and up 96% over 3 years versus Nifty's 27.71% and peer's 52.35% - outperforming both over these windows. Over 5 years, though, SBI's 134.23% trails Bank of Baroda's 223.07% gain, even though it still beats the Nifty's 38.75%. The only corporate action on record is a 10:1 stock split in November 2014, which is already reflected in the adjusted price series and does not distort any of these return figures. The stock is currently about 10% below its February 2026 peak of ₹1,206.06 - this reads as a correction within a longer uptrend, not a crash, and no demerger or spin-off needs to be added back here.
analysis.valuation_read: SBI trades at roughly 10.8x trailing earnings and about 1.5-1.6x book value. It is cheaper than private peers HDFC Bank (P/B ~2.0x) and ICICI Bank (P/B ~2.9x), but pricier than fellow public-sector peer Bank of Baroda (P/B ~0.7x), which is the comparison used in this report's chart. Why it is cheap: public-sector banks typically trade at a discount for government-ownership overhang and historically lower returns on equity versus private peers. Whether it is cheap today is less clear - sources disagree sharply on SBI's current ROE (one pegs it at 13.4%, another at 17.33%), so this should be verified on Screener before drawing a conclusion either way.
analysis.growth_read: Growth this quarter looks both margin-led and volume-led: domestic NIM expanded from 3.00% to 3.11% even as management guided to double-digit (14-15%) credit growth that it describes as diversified across retail, agri, SME and corporate segments, rather than concentrated in one book. That combination - margin improving alongside volume growth - is the more durable pattern referenced in point 7 of our house rules, as opposed to margin expansion masking flat volumes.
analysis.health_read: Profits appear to be turning into genuine balance-sheet improvement rather than just accounting gains: Gross NPA fell to 1.39% and Net NPA to 0.36%, while provisions and credit cost (0.22% versus 0.39% a year earlier) both declined in tandem - a bank padding its numbers would typically show falling NPAs alongside flat or rising provisions, not both falling together. Capital adequacy (CRAR) also strengthened to 16.09% from 14.62% YoY, helped by a ₹4,691 crore AT1 bond raise in July 2026, comfortably above the regulatory minimum. On the evidence available, business risk (asset quality) and capital risk both look well-contained currently; ROA and ROCE could not be verified from available sources and should be checked separately.
analysis.ownership_read: The Government of India remains the majority promoter at 55.45%, essentially unchanged from 55.47% the previous quarter. As a public-sector bank with a government promoter, pledging is not expected, but this report could not independently confirm a 0% pledge figure from a primary filing - treat as highly likely but unverified. FII holding rose to 11.07% from 10.81%, and DIIs hold 26.21%. Specific marquee institutional holders (e.g. LIC's exact stake) could not be verified from available sources - check the latest shareholding pattern filing directly.
strengths: Gross NPA fell to 1.39% from 1.73% a year earlier - described as the lowest level in roughly two decades
Net profit grew 14.28% YoY to ₹23,038 crore alongside NII growth of 14.69% to ₹49,143 crore in Q2 FY27
Capital adequacy (CRAR) strengthened to 16.09% from 14.62% YoY, well above the regulatory minimum, aided by a ₹4,691 crore AT1 bond raise in July 2026
Credit cost declined to 0.22% from 0.39% YoY as provisioning needs eased alongside improving asset quality
watchpoints: Stock fell roughly 5% after otherwise strong Q2 FY27 results, and MarketsMojo downgraded it to 'Sell' on valuation grounds on 4 November 2026
ROE estimates conflict sharply across sources (13.4% versus 17.33%) - this needs to be resolved on Screener before relying on either figure
5-year return of 134.23% trails peer Bank of Baroda's 223.07% despite SBI's much larger scale
Next results date, dividend record date and AGM date are not yet confirmed in available sources
analysis.one_thing: Whether SBI's standalone ROE (disputed between roughly 13.4% and 17.33% across sources) and its >3% NIM guidance hold up when Q3 FY27 results are confirmed will determine whether the current P/B discount to private-bank peers is a genuine opportunity or a fair reflection of lower returns on equity.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 operating figures (PAT, NII, NIM, GNPA/NNPA, provisions, CRAR) are cross-checked across multiple independent sources and the company's own 3 November 2026 concall, so confidence there is high. ROE, ROA, ROCE, named institutional shareholders, explicit pledge confirmation, and the next results/dividend record/AGM dates could not be reliably verified from available sources and should be checked directly on Screener or in NSE/BSE filings.
